title: The MUSE Ultra Deep Field (MUDF): VII. Probing high-redshift gas structures in the surroundings of ALMA-identified massive dusty galaxies
question: Are dusty, gas-rich galaxies found blindly with ALMA associated with metal absorbers in the MUDF quasar sightlines, and what are their properties and environments?

data.arrays: 12-m antennas (41 to 44 in band 6; 40 to 45 in band 3)
data.angular_resolution: Band 6 natural weighting 0.55" x 0.51"; band 6 tapered 2.19" x 2.39"; band 3 natural 2.5" x 2.3" at 101 GHz
data.sensitivity: Band 6: 26 uJy/beam over total bandwidth; Band 3: median 0.20 mJy/beam over 33.7 MHz (~100 km/s at 101 GHz)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the ALMA data
recipe.method: Run the ALMA pipeline scriptForPI in CASA; image band 6 with tclean (dirty natural-weighted mfs continuum, 25 km/s cubes, 90 klambda tapered continuum, cleaned images); image band 3 as dirty 100 km/s cubes
key_parameters: Pixel scale 0.08" (band 6), 0.4" (tapered), 0.3" (band 3); taper FWHM 90 klambda; band 3 channel width 100 km/s
Cleaning down to 2 sigma with 2.0" circular masks around S/N>5 sources

recipe.method: Run LineSeeker on the untapered dirty 1.2-mm continuum image (PB response >= 50%, no PB correction), extract S/N>3 detections, keep fidelity F >= 90% (S/N >= 5.0); fidelity from negative-peak statistics
key_parameters: Exclude region below 50% of maximum PB response; dirty image used without PB correction
Low-fidelity (20% <= F < 90%) candidates cross-matched to HST F140W catalog within 0.5"; no associations found
assumptions: Negative peaks are pure noise; cumulative negative-detection distribution modeled as Gaussian noise

recipe.goal: Blind line search in band 6 cubes and band 3 scans
recipe.method: Run LineSeeker on LSB and USB cubes with a matched-filter Gaussian kernel (1 to 18 channels), S/N >= 3 then F >= 90%; band 3: line search on dirty cubes plus inspection of spectra at the 1.2-mm source positions
key_parameters: Kernel width corresponds to typical line FWHM ~50-1000 km/s; source extraction restricted to PB response >= 50%
Source extraction by DBSCAN clustering of connected voxels

recipe.method: Cross-match ALMA continuum sources to the HST F140W catalog within 0.5"; take redshifts from MUSE where high-quality, otherwise from ALMA band 3 CO(3-2)
key_parameters: Match radius 0.5" (comparable to the untapered beam)

recipe.goal: Measure continuum fluxes and CO/[CI] line fluxes and luminosities
recipe.method: 1.2 mm: single-pixel peak in the ~2" tapered image, PB-rescaled, with RMS rescaled for uncertainty; CO(3-2): fit peak-pixel spectra with a Gaussian plus constant; L_CO and L'_CO from Solomon et al. 1997 relations
key_parameters: Luminosity relation L_CO = 1.04e-3 S dv nu_obs D_L^2; L'_CO = 3.25e7 S dv D_L^2 / ((1+z)^3 nu_obs^2)
assumptions: Planck cosmology for luminosity distance (H0 = 67.7, Omega_m = 0.310)

recipe.goal: SED fitting for stellar mass, SFR and extinction
recipe.method: Simultaneous fit of multiwavelength photometry (MUSE top-hat filters, HST, HAWK-I Ks, ALMA 1.2 mm) and MUSE spectra with MC-SPF with energy balance between UV absorption and FIR emission
key_parameters: Sources fitted: C1, C3, C4, C6, C7 (C2 = QSO-SE and C5 excluded)
assumptions: Bruzual & Charlot 2003 models at 40% solar metallicity, Chabrier IMF, delayed exponentially declining SFH
Double attenuation law of Calzetti et al. 2000; dust emission model of Dale et al. 2014; Byler et al. 2018 nebular lines

recipe.goal: Estimate dust masses, IR SFR and molecular gas fractions
recipe.method: Single modified black-body fit to the 1.2 mm flux for M_dust and L_IR (then SFR_IR); gas masses from CO(3-2) (via r31 and alpha_CO range) for C1, C3, C4 and from [CI] 609 um (C-to-H2 abundance) for C6; f_gas = M_H2/(M_H2+M*)
key_parameters: T_dust = 32 K, beta = 1.8; C5 and C2 excluded from dust masses
assumptions: r31 = 0.80 +/- 0.14; alpha_CO from 0.8 to 4.3 Msun/(K km/s pc^2)

recipe.method: Match ALMA-selected and HST-selected galaxies with absorbers in velocity space within |dv| <= 500 km/s in either quasar sightline; count association rate
key_parameters: Redshift accuracy of ALMA-selected galaxies dv <~ 60 km/s
assumptions: Absorber redshift taken from the component with the largest column density

recipe.method: Identify groups with friends-of-friends (+-500 km/s); count HST-selected galaxies within +-250 km/s and within a radius equal to the QSO impact parameter, divide by MUSE-coverage-corrected area, compare surface density with absorber EW and fit a linear model
key_parameters: Mg II used for C1, C6, C7; Al II for C3

score_reason: Observing setup, CASA versions, imaging options, LineSeeker thresholds, fitting method and many numeric results are given, but several imaging parameters, the source table, and the optical catalogs and absorber table (external) are not reproducible from this paper alone.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA part (continuum source search, CO(3-2) fluxes, luminosities, redshifts) has numeric answers and a mostly complete recipe on archive projects that are linked to the paper; the SED and absorber association parts need external catalogs.
